THE POSTGRAD (Sir George Williams University alumni magazine), THREE ISSUES
Class notes as a source of camp staffing, 1955-1966

Found 2026-09-07 by the accounted sweep of rma-concordia-publications (p_479).
None of the three was in sources.json. Each item has ONE _djvu.txt (checked).

  1955  postgrad-1955-april   Vol. 11 No. 1, Easter Issue        119,799 chars
        Kanawana 0, Otoreke 1
  1957  postgrad-1957-oct     Vol. 13 No. 3, Thanksgiving Issue   78,640 chars
        Kanawana 2, Otoreke 0
  1966  postgrad-1966-summer-hall-building-issue
        Vol. 22 No. 2, Summer 1966, The Building Issue           101,407 chars
        Kanawana 0, Otoreke 1

WHY AN ALUMNI MAGAZINE IS WORTH SWEEPING. Its class notes record where graduates
went, in their own words, year by year. For a camp staffed out of a college that
is a roster nobody at the camp ever wrote — the same channel the Sir George
yearbooks and the McGill Daily advertisements show from other angles.

===============================================================================
1966: A NAMED DIRECTOR OF CAMP OTOREKE, AND AN UNLIKELY ROUTE TO THE JOB
===============================================================================

  "ROBERT D. (BOB) SALLERY, B.A. '62, VALEDICTORIAN, CLASS OF '62 is now back in
  Montreal and WILL TAKE OVER THE POSITION OF DIRECTOR OF CAMP OTOREKE. After
  Sir George Bob went to Southern Illinois University with a teaching
  assistantship and tuition scholarship. FROM SEPTEMBER '63 TO SEPTEMBER '65 HE
  WAS IN BEIRUT, LEBANON WITH THE UNITED NATIONS RELIEF AND WORKS AGENCY FOR
  PALESTINE ARAB REFUGEES (UNRWA) RESPONSIBLE FOR THE DEVELOPMENT AND SUPERVISION
  OF 48 REFUGEE YOUTH ACTIVITY CENTRES scattered throughout Lebanon, Jordan,
  Syria and the Gaza Strip. Developed program for Canadian Y.M.C.A. summer
  service volunteers in the Middle East. 22 Canadian students (including 3
  Georgians) have participated on a volunteer basis. In 1965 Bob was graduated
  from the American University of Beirut with an M.A. in Social Psychology. He
  has spent the last year at Dalhousie University on a doctoral program. Bob and
  his wife Janet Marilyn (née Pickford of Westmount) have one daughter Marilyn
  and are expecting another momentarily."

wiki/site/camp-otoreke.md is thin on named directors: McGerrigle from the
mid-1930s, Ron Hupfield by 1942 (established earlier today), George N. Barker at
the ski lodge in 1943, and the 1967 absorption into Downtown Branch. Sallery
fills 1966, the year before that absorption.

AND THE ROUTE IS THE STORY. A man who had spent two years running forty-eight
refugee youth centres across four Middle Eastern territories, and built the
Y's own Canadian volunteer pipeline into them, came home to run a family camp
in the Laurentians. The Y.M.C.A. connection is explicit and it runs both ways:
he developed the programme that sent 22 Canadian students, three of them Sir
George men, to the Middle East as YMCA summer service volunteers.

===============================================================================
1957: TWO SIR GEORGE GRADUATES AT KAMP KANAWANA, FROM THE CLASS NOTES
===============================================================================

  "GEORGE E. CLIFFORD, B.A. — is a student at McGill U. — faculty of Divinity —
  THIS SUMMER HE WILL BE AT Y.M.C.A. KAMP KANAWANA IN ST. SAUVEUR DES MONTS,
  QUE."

  "DAVID J. CARSON, B.A. — PRESENTLY AT THE Y.M.C.A. KAMP KANAWANA IN ST.
  SAUVEUR, QUE. He will be working at the Bell Telephone, Traffic Dept."

Neither name occurs anywhere else in this project (greped across wiki/,
kb/facts.json, project-docs/ and sources/sources.json before writing: zero).
They are not directors and the notes give no role, so what they document is the
ordinary case rather than the notable one — two graduates of the same college in
the same season at the same camp, one heading into divinity and one into the
telephone company. That is the Sir George pipeline working at the level it
normally worked at, in a year (1957) that falls inside Murray B. Shantz's
Kanawana directorship.

===============================================================================
1955: "OTOREKE SCHOOL, QUE." — RECORDED AS A QUESTION, NOT A FACT
===============================================================================

From a report of a model United Nations Security Council session staged in the
YWCA building at 1355 Dorchester St W in February 1955, with nine Canadian
schools and colleges, one American college and the local United Nations
Association playing the eleven council members, in four languages, presided over
by Rene Pouliot, "in real life technical adviser to the International Civil
Aviation Organization in Montreal":

  "Among the groups taking part in the debate were Assumption College, Windsor,
  Ont., (Belgium); Sir George Williams Day College (Peru); OTOREKE SCHOOL, QUE.
  (BRAZIL); United Nations Association (Turkey); University of Toronto (United
  Kingdom); University of Montreal (France); Sir George Williams Evening College
  (Iran); Royal Military College Kingston (New Zealand); and Macdonald Teachers
  College."

WHAT TO DO WITH THIS. Every other delegation is a real institution, named
precisely, so the list is not careless. But nothing in this project knows of an
"Otoreke School," and the YMCA's Camp Otoreke is a summer camp, not a school
sending a delegation to a February debate in Montreal. Three readings, none
adopted here:

  (a) an OCR or editorial garble of another institution's name;
  (b) a school that used the Otoreke site, which would fit the off-season and
      conference use camp-otoreke.md documents from other years;
  (c) a distinct institution that happens to share the name.

This is written into the wiki as an open question with the quotation attached,
because a fourth possibility — that somebody later reads "Otoreke School" as
established fact — is the one worth guarding against.
